directAnswer: To reset a Git merge, use the command 'git reset --merge' or 'git reset --hard HEAD' depending on whether you want to keep the changes or discard them.
summary: This guide provides steps to reset a Git merge and outlines important considerations.

sections.heading: Understanding Git Merge
sections.body: A Git merge combines changes from different branches. If conflicts arise or you decide not to proceed, resetting the merge can help.

sections.heading: Reset Options
sections.body: You can choose to keep changes with 'git reset --merge' or discard them with 'git reset --hard HEAD'. Choose based on your needs.

steps.title: Check Current Status
steps.detail: Run 'git status' to see the current state of your repository and confirm that you are in a merge conflict.

steps.title: Reset the Merge
steps.detail: Use 'git reset --merge' to keep changes or 'git reset --hard HEAD' to discard changes. Note that '--hard' will erase uncommitted changes.

steps.title: Verify the Reset
steps.detail: Run 'git status' again to ensure that the repository is back to its previous state.

faqs.question: What happens to my changes after a hard reset?
faqs.answer: A hard reset will permanently discard all uncommitted changes, so ensure you have backups if needed.

faqs.question: Can I recover discarded changes after a hard reset?
faqs.answer: Generally, no. Once a hard reset is performed, the changes are lost unless you have a backup or they were committed.

faqs.question: Is there a way to abort a merge without resetting?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can use 'git merge --abort' to stop the merge process if you haven't committed yet.

caveats: Be cautious with 'git reset --hard' as it will erase all uncommitted changes.
Always ensure you are on the correct branch before performing a reset.
